Session 7 · Mods · 01
The big idea
A mod is code that runs inside Claude Code
Shipped in v2.1.287 (1 Oct 2026). Hooks, skills and MCP work from outside. A mod runs inside, so it can draw, step into a tool call, or answer it.

Markdown

Session 7 · Mods · 02
How a mod works
Three files make a mod
A mod is a plugin with a hooks module. Claude Code calls its register function once and hands it on().
files
first-mod/
├── .claude-plugin/
│ └── plugin.json
└── hooks/
    ├── hooks.json
    └── register.js
hooks/register.js
let calls = 0
export function register(on) {
  on('tool.call', async ($, e, next) => {
    calls += 1
    $.ui.invalidate('ui.render')
    return next(e)
  })
  on('ui.render', { component: 'Spinner' },
    async ($, e, next) => next({ ...e,
      props: { ...e.props,
        suffix: ' · tool calls: ' + calls }}))
}
Official example
Session 7 · Mods · 03
React to events
Every hook can observe, rewrite or answer
Claude Code runs your hook before it acts. It passes $ (the mods API), e (the event) and next (the rest of the chain).
Observe
Note what happens, then call next(e) unchanged
Rewrite
Change the event, then pass it on: next({...e})
Answer
Handle it yourself and skip the default, like refusing a command
Events the nine mods use
session.start
prompt.submit
tool.call
agent.spawn
turn.start
turn.step
turn.complete
command.run
ui.render
ui.close

Session 7 · Mods · 05
Install guide
Three ways to load a mod
inside Claude Code
# from a marketplace, inside a session
/plugin marketplace add owner/repo
/plugin install name@marketplace
/reload-plugins
 
# one session, from a folder
claude --plugin-dir ./my-mod
~/.claude/settings.json
{ "env": {
  "CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_DIRS":
    "~/mods/a:~/mods/b"
} }
Check: claude --version must be 2.1.287 or later. Run /plugin and look for the dim "N mods active" line.

Mod 01 · savvy-progress
Savvy Progress shows your subagents at work
A progress bar above the prompt and a live panel of every subagent. Built for the savvy-flow skill, useful with any subagents.
Hooks it uses
session.start
command.run
tool.call
agent.spawn
turn.step
turn.complete
ui.render
Progress bar
Flow title, phase, accepted tasks out of planned, and a crew-size button that opens the panel
/agents-info panel
Running, finished and planned subagents with model, effort, progress, context, cost and time
Two report tools
progress for the orchestrator, step for workers. A silent worker shows its context fill in grey

Mod 02 · filetree
Filetree shows the files Claude touches
An IDE-style file tree in the right sidebar. Files shimmer purple on reads and searches, orange on writes, green on commits.
Needs
Terminal: fullscreen layout (/tui fullscreen) and 110+ columns. Desktop app docks it on its own. /filetree reopens it, /filetree <path> pins a folder.
Git at a glance
Status colour per file, +N −N lines on modified files, branch and ahead/behind in the header
Selection is context
The selected file goes to Claude through a prompt.submit hook; @path in a prompt reveals it
Settings in /config
Claude activity, Follow Claude, right column (date, age, size), Open with: preview

Mod 03 · replay-theater
Replay Theater replays the last turn's edits
It records every file edit Claude makes in a turn. /replay steps through the diffs one at a time in a docked pane.
validate (trimmed)
$ claude plugin validate replay-theater
hooks: session.start,
  command.run{command=replay},
  tool.call, turn.start, turn.complete,
  ui.render{component=Pane}, ui.close
calls: $.command.register,
  $.fs.exists, $.fs.read, $.ui.open
Records
tool.call plus turn.start and turn.complete capture each edit of the turn
/replay
command.run registers the command; the pane shows one diff per step
Read-only
Its calls read files and draw. It starts no programs and makes no network calls

Mod 04 · blast-radius
Blast Radius holds risky commands for review
Before rm -rf, git reset --hard, git push --force or a migration runs, it opens a pane listing what would change.
validate (trimmed)
$ claude plugin validate blast-radius
hooks: tool.call{tool=Bash},
  ui.render{component=Pane},
  ui.render{component=AbovePrompt}
calls: $.clock.now, $.process.run,
  $.session.cwd, $.ui.open,
  $.ui.resolve, $.ui.toast
Catches
A tool.call hook on Bash only, matching destructive commands
Explains
Lists the files and refs the command would hit, using $.process.run
Decides
Proceed lets the call through. Cancel answers it, so the command never runs
Anthropic sample
Guard

Mod 05 · you-should-know
You Should Know watches long tasks for you
A built-in mod. A side agent watches while Claude works on longer tasks and shows a short note above the prompt.
Good to know
--safe-mode, --bare and disableAllHooks do not stop built-in mods. Turn it off in /plugin. Its source is not public, unlike diff and agents-md.
Off by default
Enable with /plugin enable cc-plugin-you-should-know@builtin
Says who decided
Since v2.1.288 notes say "we", "the main agent" or "you"
Costs usage
The side agent makes model calls on your plan or API key. No amount published
Built-in
Side agent

Session 7 · Mods · 28
Mod 07 · cache-tax
Cache Tax keeps the prompt cache warm
Step away and the prompt cache goes cold, so the next send rewrites it. Cache Tax warms it during breaks and warns first.
Needs
Claude Code 2.1.287+, a one-hour cache, and Claude Code left running while you are away.
Keep warm
While armed, a row with the Cache Tax cube shows above the prompt
/cache-tax
Current cache estimate, warming window and this session's cold-write tally
Guard
By default it refuses a cold send once with the estimated cost. The resend goes through
Community mod
Band + guard

Mod 08 · skins
Claude Skins redraws the transcript itself
It replaces what Claude Code draws: tool rows get icons, diffs and tables become cards, and there are fifteen themes.
Hooks it uses
ui.render
tool rows
Spinner
usage band
Every skin has light and dark and follows Claude Code's theme.
Tool rows
Each tool call row gets an icon and a cleaner layout
Cards
Diffs, tables and Mermaid charts render as cards in the transcript
Themes
/skin <name> switches, e.g. /skin calm. Fifteen to pick from

Mod 09 · terminal-browser
Terminal Browser runs Chromium beside Claude
A real browser that renders inside your terminal. Claude can open it in a split pane and drive it from the CLI.
How it renders
Electron offscreen rendering reads Chromium pixels; the kitty graphics protocol draws them in Ghostty, kitty, VS Code and more.
Split pane
terminal-browser --split right opens it next to your agent
Agent control
terminal-browser action: an agent-browser compatible CLI for open browsers
Over SSH
terminal-browser --ssh previews sites running on a remote machine
Community
Plugin + CLI
